acceptance.criterion: Watch for the scroll-ownership consequence on every screen (hub ADR-0042 §Consequences): a screen giving up its scroller loses scroll observation and control. Check before migrating, not after
acceptance.evidence: grep -n "(scroll)|scrollTop|scrollIntoView|scrollTo" milestones.ts/.html: one live site, `centerTodayMarker()` (milestones.ts:366), which writes `list.scrollTop` directly against its own ViewChild -- no ScreenChromeService.requestScrollReset() call anywhere in this screen (grep confirms), so the layout's existing scroll-to-top-only control channel is not implicated. Measured in a real browser rather than reasoned out, per this task's explicit instruction: on mobile (360px) TODAY, before any change in this slice, `.list`'s computed `overflow-y` is `visible` (no overflow declared below 900px) and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` (2792 === 2792, `main` -- not `.list` -- is the real scroller); writing `list.scrollTop = 999` and reading it back gives `0` -- the write is **already a silent no-op on mobile, before this slice touched anything**. This is a pre-existing defect (the "Today" marker never centers into view on a phone), not a regression this slice introduced -- this slice makes no change to `.list`, to mobile CSS, or to `centerTodayMarker()` itself. At >=900px (also measured, before any route change): `.list` overflow-y is `auto`, scrollHeight 2812 > clientHeight 627, and the write-then-read round-trips correctly (200 written, 200 read back) -- centering already works on desktop today. This finding is load-bearing for the escalation below: Option A there (letting `.screen-scroll` take over `.list`'s own scrolling) would additionally regress the desktop case from working to no-op, which the current code does not do.
acceptance.notes: Reported as a risk (a pre-existing mobile defect this slice did not cause and was not authorized to fix unilaterally, since fixing it would mean deciding whether centering should even attempt anything on a screen where the whole page scrolls) rather than fixed here.

risks.risk: centerTodayMarker() (milestones.ts:366)'s `list.scrollTop` write is already a silent no-op on mobile (<900px) today, independent of anything in this or any future T343 slice -- `.list` declares no `overflow` below 900px, so it is not a scroll container there and the write is clamped to 0. The "Today" marker therefore never centers into view on a phone; on first load a couple opening /milestones on mobile sees whatever position the DOM naturally renders at, not the marker scrolled into view. Not fixed here: fixing it would require deciding what "center" even means on a screen where main (not .list) is the real mobile scroller -- e.g. scrolling main to the marker's offsetTop instead -- which is a real, if small, product/UX decision (does the couple want the page to jump on load?) this task was not asked to make, and is entangled with (though not blocked by) the master-detail decision below: whichever option is chosen, .list stays the real desktop scroller either way, but only a deliberate mobile-specific fix would ever make the marker centre on a phone.

decisions_needed.question: milestones has a genuine, already-working two-pane master-detail layout at >=900px: `.list` and `.detail-body` each scroll independently and are not nested inside one another (confirmed by measurement: `.list` overflow-y auto, scrollHeight 2812 > clientHeight 627; `.detail-body` overflow-y auto, independently scrollable; `main`'s own scrollHeight === clientHeight today, i.e. main never actually overflows because :host's height:100% + flex/min-height:0 discipline already bounds it exactly). ADR-0043 §5 names milestones as `screenScroll: 'lg'` but does not say what happens to these two panes once that flag is set and PrivateLayout's `.screen-scroll` wrapper (around the whole routed component) gets `screen-scroll()`'s own `flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto`. seating-plan has the identical shape (`.unassigned-body`, `.tables`), so the answer applies to both.
options: A -- screen-scroll() takes over: set screenScroll:'lg' AND strip .list/.detail-body's own overflow-y:auto so PrivateLayout's .screen-scroll wrapper becomes the sole scroller for the whole routed component. Cost: destroys the master-detail UX -- a long list would carry the detail pane's action buttons off-screen while scrolling instead of keeping them visible, the opposite of what a fixed detail pane is for. Measured to also regress centerTodayMarker()'s desktop behaviour, which works correctly today (list.scrollTop round-trips 200->200) -- under this option .list would no longer be a scroll container at all, so the write would go from working to a silent no-op on desktop too, not just remain broken on mobile. No precedent for this in the phase: guest-manager/config-manager never make the layout's wrapper absorb a screen's own internal, non-page-level regions.

B -- screen-scroll() applies to an inert wrapper, panes keep their own scrollers: set screenScroll:'lg' per ADR-0043 §5, leave .list/.detail-body's declarations exactly as they are today. Since :host's existing height:100% + flex/min-height:0 chain already bounds the component exactly within main's box (measured: main never overflows even today, before this flag exists), .screen-scroll's own screen-scroll() mixin ends up genuinely inert once applied -- a scroll container with zero scrollable range. Its real effect is removing main's own live-but-currently-inert overflow-y:auto (the ADR-0041 §4 hazard class: a box a focus event could shift, even with nothing currently overflowing it) and replacing it with .screen-scroll's equally inert one, purely so main stops being a scroll container the moment this screen is active. Cost: a second, also-inert scroll container is introduced where arguably none is needed (mild code smell, no functional cost); T352 risks[1]'s own open item -- no live route has proven :host's height:100% still resolves correctly with .screen-scroll's own flex/min-height:0 sitting between main and :host, since this was previously only checked by hand-applying classes to /schedule, a screen with no internal shell of its own.
decisions_needed.recommendation: Option B. It matches ADR-0043 §5's own naming of the route flag, is consistent with this file's own T347-authored header comment already sanctioning `.detail-body` as "a separate, independent scroller ... not nested ... not a second competing scroller on the same axis", and does not regress anything that works today (centerTodayMarker's desktop behaviour, or the master-detail UX itself). Option A actively breaks both. The only real cost of B is unverified plumbing (T352's own open item) rather than a design trade-off, and that is exactly what a real-route Playwright spec (deferred to `remaining[]`) would settle once this is decided.
